description: A pair of green leather pointed shoes with long upturned curled gold toes and gold stitching, decorated with heraldic shields (lions, fleurs-de-lis, crown) and a buckled strap, worn by a person in dark blue hose standing on a grey stone floor. Oil-painting style filling the image edge to edge, no border or frame. No letters or numbers; only a small sparkle logo in the bottom-right corner. Nothing graphic. Era cues point to medieval poulaines.
reason: Shows medieval poulaine shoes with heraldic shields, but the card is the ancient Egyptian Mehen snake board game (about 3000 BCE). The footwear and heraldry are a clear anachronism and show nothing of the game, its spiral snake board, marble pieces or lions.
